2027-03-05.title: Friday of the fourth week of the Great Fast · Anniversary of the enthronement of our Major Archbishop-Catholicos
2027-03-05.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malankara Panchangam; the Gospel verses are unclear in the source and are read here as John 10:14–16, verify locally)
readings: God hears the boy in the wilderness
Stand firm in your faith; let all that you do be done in love
I am the good shepherd; other sheep I have
2027-03-05.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), fourth week. Anniversary of the enthronement of Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis Catholicos as Major Archbishop-Catholicos (2007). The Panchangam's Gospel reference for this day is unclear in the source text (it may be John 10:1–16 or John 10:14–16); check your parish lectionary. For many families it is also the First Friday of the month.
2027-03-05.verse: Do not be afraid; for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
theo: Yesterday Hagar and Ishmael were sent into the wilderness; today we follow them there. The water runs out. Hagar lays the boy under a bush and goes a bowshot away, “for she said, ‘Do not let me look on the death of the child.’ And as she sat opposite him, she lifted up her voice and wept.” It is one of the loneliest scenes in the Bible: a foreign slave woman, cast out, with a dying child, in a desert. And then: “God heard the voice of the boy; and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, and said to her, ‘What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid; for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.’” The name Ishmael means “God hears.” God hears him not after he is brought back to Abraham's tent, but “where he is,” under the bush in the desert. “Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water.” The well had been there all along; she needed God to open her eyes. In the Great Fast many of us feel that our water skin is empty. The Lord who heard Ishmael hears us where we are.

The Gospel shows us the Shepherd who hears and knows: “I am the good shepherd. I know my own and my own know me, just as the Father knows me and I know the Father. And I lay down my life for the sheep. I have other sheep that do not belong to this fold. I must bring them also, and they will listen to my voice. So there will be one flock, one shepherd.” Ishmael was outside the tent, but not outside God's care; Christ's heart reaches the sheep outside the fold, and he lays down his life to gather them. St Gregory the Great taught that “I know my own” means: I love them; and “my own know me” means: they obey me in love, for one who does not love does not yet truly know (in substance). Today our Church gives thanks for the anniversary of the enthronement of our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis, in 2007. We pray that he may be a shepherd after the heart of Christ, who knows his flock and seeks those far away. And Paul's farewell to the Corinthians becomes our prayer for all shepherds and for ourselves: “Keep alert, stand firm in your faith, be courageous, be strong. Let all that you do be done in love.” He ends with the ancient cry of the Church in Aramaic, which the NRSV renders: “Our Lord, come!”
outline: Ask: have you ever felt that no one could hear you?
Point 1 · God has heard the voice of the boy
Hagar's tears and the well in the desert.
Point 2 · Stand firm, do all in love
Paul's farewell and the cry “Our Lord, come!”
The Good Shepherd and our Catholicos.
“God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.”
live: In a situation where you feel dry and helpless, ask God today to show you the “well” that is already near you: a person, a sacrament, a word of Scripture.
Pray today for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos on the anniversary of his enthronement, and for your own bishop and parish priest.
2027-03-05.prayer: God who hears, you heard the voice of the boy Ishmael under the bush in the wilderness, and you opened Hagar's eyes to see the well of water. Hear us where we are, in our dryness and our fears. Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you know your own and lay down your life for them; bring home the sheep that are far away, and make us one flock under one shepherd. Bless our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis, on the anniversary of his enthronement; keep him alert and firm in faith, courageous and strong, doing all things in love. Our Lord, come! Amen.
altar: On this Friday of the Fast the Good Shepherd who laid down his life is offered at the altar; the Church's prayer “Our Lord, come!” is answered each time he comes, truly present, in the Holy Qurbono.

quick: In the wilderness God heard the voice of the boy Ishmael and opened Hagar's eyes to a well of water.
Paul says: keep alert, stand firm in faith, be courageous and strong; let all that you do be done in love.
Jesus, the Good Shepherd, knows his own, lays down his life, and gathers other sheep into one flock.
2027-03-05.action: Pray today for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and for your bishop.
2027-03-05.question: Where do I need God to open my eyes to a well I have not seen?

family.explain: Hagar and her little boy were alone in the desert with no water. The boy was crying, and Hagar was crying too. But God heard the boy crying, and God showed Hagar a well of water. God hears us too, wherever we are. Today we also pray for our Catholicos, the shepherd of our Church.
family.intention: We pray for children who are thirsty, hungry or alone, and for our Catholicos.
family.ask: Ask: “When did God help us when we felt alone?”

illus: A young nurse from Mavelikara, newly arrived in a hospital in a northern European city, found herself on night duty in a ward where no one spoke Malayalam and she understood half of what was said. One night, after a patient died, she sat in the staff room and cried. A cleaner, an old woman from the Philippines, came in, said nothing, and put a cup of tea and a small holy card of the Good Shepherd beside her. The next Sunday the cleaner took her to a Mass where she found three other nurses from Kerala. She says: I was looking for a way home. God showed me the well that was already there.

pm.open: Lord, you hear us where we are. Open our eyes to see your gifts, and make us one flock under you, the Good Shepherd. Amen.
share: God has heard the voice of the boy where he is (Genesis 21:17). Do I believe God hears me even in my wilderness?
Let all that you do be done in love (1 Corinthians 16:14). Which of my daily tasks needs more love?
I know my own and my own know me (John 10:14). How well do I know the voice of the Good Shepherd?
pm.resp: Lord, hear us where we are.
interc: For Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis, our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, on the anniversary of his enthronement.
For mothers and children in deserts of poverty, war and exile.
For migrants and those working far from home.
For those who have drifted from the Church, the sheep outside the fold.
For unity among all Christians, one flock under one shepherd.
pm.close: Father, you heard Ishmael's cry and you sent your Son to gather all your scattered children. Bless the shepherds of your Church, open our eyes to your gifts, and keep us firm in faith and generous in love until Christ comes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hagar and her son are in the wilderness, and the water is gone. She lays the boy under a bush and weeps (Genesis 21:15–16). It is one of the loneliest scenes in Scripture.

But God heard the voice of the boy; and the angel said: do not be afraid; for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is. Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water (Genesis 21:17, 19). God hears us where we are, not only when we are where we ought to be.

Jesus says: I am the good shepherd. I know my own and my own know me. I have other sheep that do not belong to this fold; so there will be one flock, one shepherd (John 10:14, 16). Today we pray for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos on the anniversary of his enthronement, that he may shepherd us with the heart of Christ.
And Paul tells us all: keep alert, stand firm in your faith, be courageous, be strong. Let all that you do be done in love (1 Corinthians 16:13–14). Amen.
kids: Children, a little boy named Ishmael was crying in the desert because he was thirsty. God heard him! And God showed his mother a well full of water. Ishmael's name means “God hears.” God hears you too, every time you pray, wherever you are. Today let us also pray for our Catholicos, the shepherd of our Church.

intro: Theme: “God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.”
Ishmael in the desert, Paul's farewell, and the Good Shepherd who gathers one flock; on the anniversary of our Catholicos' enthronement.

sub: God opens her eyes to the well.
q: This poor soul cried, and was heard by the Lord, and was saved from every trouble.
Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
points.apply: Bring your driest place to God in prayer every day this week and ask him to open your eyes.

points.h: Stand firm, do all in love
q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
Above all, clothe yourselves with love, which binds everything together in perfect harmony.
points.apply: Choose one duty you do grudgingly and do it this week with love.

q: I will set up over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he shall feed them: he shall feed them and be their shepherd.
There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to the one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
points.apply: Pray daily for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and for Christian unity.

concl: God hears the cry of the outcast and opens eyes to hidden wells.
The Good Shepherd gathers his flock through shepherds who stand firm and do all in love.
2027-03-05.resolve: Trust that God hears you where you are, and pray every day for the shepherds of the Church.
